html:
The Demerara rebellion was a rising of more than ten thousand enslaved people in the British colony of Demerara, now part of Guyana, in August 1823.

Rumours spread that Britain had freed the slaves and the planters were hiding it. Led by Jack Gladstone and his father Quamina, a deacon of a mission chapel, the enslaved on dozens of plantations locked up their masters and demanded their freedom. There was little killing by the rebels, but soldiers and militia shot hundreds, and many leaders were hanged.

The English missionary John Smith was condemned to death for encouraging the revolt and died in prison. His case caused anger in Britain and strengthened the campaign that led to the Slavery Abolition Act of 1833. Like the earlier Berbice revolt, it is part of the founding story of Guyana, on the same sugar coast as its capital, Georgetown.
sum: The Demerara rebellion was a rising of more than ten thousand enslaved people in the British colony of Demerara, now part of Guyana, in August 1823.
